newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sets up export credit agency.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sets up export credit agency.

text.p: Brazil will set up an export credit agency by mid-year after several local banks and French export guarantee agency Coface signed a partnership, Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles said.

Dornelles said at a ceremony in Brasilia's Presidential Palace that export guarantees would open up new markets for large Brazilian exporters and would also make it possible for smaller firms to start selling abroad.
"This is going to boost Brazilian exports," Dornelles said.
Coface will hold a 25 percent stake in the new agency.
Its Brazilian partners, each with an 11 percent take, are state-run Banco do Brasil, insurance firms Companhia Seguros Minas Brasil and Sul America Seguros, and private banks Bradesco and Bamerindus.
The remaining 20 percent stake in the agency was open for bids, Dornelles said.
Dornelles expected the agency to be up and running by the middle of the year and that it would insure Brazilian exports against commercial and political risks.

Brazil decided last year to revive export insurance in a bid to revive its flagging exports and plug a widening trade gap, which hit $5.54 billion last year and seems set to reach at least $8.0 billion in 1997.
